Specifically, you have received [redacted] donors of umbilical cord blood units since January 2019 from your main supplier located in [redacted] which is an area identified as an active transmission risk area. From the umbilical cord blood units you received, you produced [redacted] of which [redacted] vial were further distributed. A. For example, FDA has identified Zika virus (ZIKV) as a relevant communicable disease agent or disease (RCDAD) under 21 CFR 127l.3(r)(2). Therefore, review of relevant medical records, as defined in 21 CFR 12 71. 3 (s), must indicate that a potential donor is free from risk factors for, or clinical evidence of, ZlKV infection for the purpose of determining donor eligibility. Form DT-001 "Donor Risk Assessment Interview" utilized by your main supplier of umbilical cord blood located in [redacted] does not include the full complement of questions required to assess a donor's relevant communicable disease risk as it relates to ZIKV. Form DT-001 only asks donors "Have you ever been diagnosed with or suspected of having dengue, chikungunya or Zika virus." The following questions are missing: 1. Whether the donor has resided in or traveled to an area with increased risk for Zika virus transmission at any point during pregnancy or 2. Had sex at any point during pregnancy with a person who has resided in or traveled to an area with increased risk for Zika virus transmission or 3. Had sex at any point during pregnancy with a person who had a medical diagnosis of ZIKV infection. B. The firm accepted deficient relevant medical records from their umbilical cord blood supplier that were subsequently used evaluate donor eligibility. Form DT-001 "Donor Risk Assessment Interview" does not include complete and/or accurate screening questions related to the following conditions and behaviors that increase a donor's relevant communicable disease risk.
